claims.text: A read-only provider can neither edit files nor run tests. Any change it proposes is advisory: it is moved into ``handoff.suggestions`` and the mutating fields are forced empty so nothing can be auto-applied.
claims.why: The code checks self.caps.can_write; if False, it moves proposed files to handoff.suggested_files and clears files_changed and tests_run.

claims.text: A model that cannot write cannot legitimately be "done" applying a change; downgrade to advisory review.
claims.why: The code sets report['status'] = 'needs_review' when original status was 'done'.

observations.what: Class attribute 'caps' is declared but not typed; should be type hinted as ProviderCapabilities.
In _enforce_read_only, the variable name 'handoff' shadows the outer 'handoff' parameter? No, it's local. But the code uses 'handoff' as dict variable, then assigns to report['handoff']. No issues.
The method name '_enforce_read_only' suggests it enforces read-only policy, but it only modifies the report; it does not raise errors or validate inputs.
